title: A safe new table
prompt: Create a table named bookings with id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, trail_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES trails(id), and people INTEGER with CHECK (people > 0). Add one booking: id 1, trail 1, 4 people.

check.sql: SELECT i.name, i."notnull", i.pk, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_foreign_key_list('bookings')) AS foreign_keys, (SELECT instr(upper(sql), 'CHECK') > 0 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'bookings') AS has_check, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bookings) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trails) AS total_rows FROM pragma_table_info('bookings') i ORDER BY i.cid;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM trails; INSERT INTO trails VALUES (7, 'Birch Walk', 'West', 3.1, 40), (8, 'High Moor', 'East', 12.6, 610), (9, 'Crag Top', 'North', 6.0, 900);

solutions: CREATE TABLE bookings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, trail_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES trails(id), people INTEGER CHECK (people > 0)); INSERT INTO bookings VALUES (1, 1, 4);

wrongSolutions.sql: CREATE TABLE bookings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, trail_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES trails(id), people INTEGER); INSERT INTO bookings VALUES (1, 1, 4);
CREATE TABLE bookings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, trail_id INTEGER, people INTEGER CHECK (people > 0)); INSERT INTO bookings VALUES (1, 1, 4);

title: Normalise the tags
prompt: Contacts' cities repeat. Create a table cities with id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and name TEXT UNIQUE, filled with each known city. Then add a city_id column to contacts, and set it from the new table.
hints: CREATE, INSERT with DISTINCT, ALTER, and UPDATE.

check.sql: SELECT c.id, ci.name FROM contacts c JOIN cities ci ON ci.id = c.city_id ORDER BY c.id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: CREATE TABLE cities (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT UNIQUE); INSERT INTO cities (name) SELECT DISTINCT city FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE contacts ADD COLUMN city_id INTEGER; UPDATE contacts SET city_id = (SELECT id FROM cities WHERE cities.name = contacts.city);

wrongSolutions.sql: CREATE TABLE cities (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT UNIQUE); INSERT INTO cities (name) SELECT DISTINCT city FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE contacts ADD COLUMN city_id INTEGER;
CREATE TABLE cities (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT UNIQUE); ALTER TABLE contacts ADD COLUMN city_id INTEGER;

title: Sales view
prompt: Create a view named sales with order_id, customer name as customer, product name as product, and quantity times price as line_total.

check.sql: SELECT order_id, customer, product, line_total FROM sales ORDER BY order_id, product;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: CREATE VIEW sales AS SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer, p.name AS product, i.quantity * p.price AS line_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: CREATE VIEW sales AS SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer, p.name AS product, p.price AS line_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

CREATE VIEW sales AS SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer, i.product_id AS product, i.quantity * p.price AS line_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

title: Tune a lookup
prompt: Queries often filter employees by department_id and sort by salary. Create a composite index named idx_dept_salary on (department_id, salary).

check.sql: SELECT c.seqno, c.name FROM pragma_index_info('idx_dept_salary') c ORDER BY c.seqno;

solutions: CREATE INDEX idx_dept_salary ON employees (department_id, salary);

wrongSolutions.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_dept_salary ON employees (salary, department_id);

title: Team size with reports
prompt: For the employee with no manager, show their name and the total number of people below them at any depth as team_size.
hints: Walk down, then count all but the top.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT id, id AS root FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, t.root FROM employees e JOIN t ON e.manager_id = t.id) SELECT m.name, COUNT(*) - 1 AS team_size FROM t JOIN employees m ON m.id = t.root GROUP BY m.id, m.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT m.name, COUNT(*) AS team_size FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id WHERE m.manager_id IS NULL GROUP BY m.id, m.name;

WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT id, id AS root FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, t.root FROM employees e JOIN t ON e.manager_id = t.id) SELECT m.name, COUNT(*) AS team_size FROM t JOIN employees m ON m.id = t.root GROUP BY m.id, m.name;
